summary: Jan-Ulrich Sobisch specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under David P. Jackson, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Nubpa Rinpoche, and held posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, the University of Copenhagen (2003–2006), Hamburg, and Munich.
Jane Bunnag works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of London in 1969, studying under supervisors Nathaniel Tarn and Barbara E. Ward.
Jane Caple is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She has held posts at the University of Leeds and at the University of Manchester, where she is attested as a Research Fellow in 2026.

Jane Ellen Harrison (1850–1928) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. She studied at Cheltenham Ladies' College (~1870–1874), Newnham College (~1874–1879), and under Robert Alexander Neil, later holding a post at the University of Cambridge (~1898–1922).
Jane-Marie Law specializes in Japanology and religious studies. At Cornell University, she served as Director of Graduate Studies (attested 2008) and Associate Professor (attested 2026).

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who earned her BA, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley (~1968–1981). Her posts include Amherst College (1987–2001) and Harvard University as Hershey Professor of Buddhist Studies (2001).

Janet R. Goodwin specializes in Japanology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at UC Berkeley under Delmer M. Brown and Britten Dean, and held posts attested in 1994 at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu.
Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota, as well as teachers Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Frances Wilson.

Janice Dean Willis specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Cornell (~1965–1971) and Columbia (~1972–1976) under Alex Wayman and Yeshe Thubten, later holding posts at Wesleyan University (1977–2013) and Agnes Scott College (2014–2020).

Janice Leoshko works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under Susan L. Huntington and became Professor Emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

Jann Ronis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under David Germano, Jeffrey Hopkins, and Sonam Tenpa, and held an attested post there in 2007.
Jared Rhoton (1941–1993) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sakya Trizin and completed his dissertation at Columbia University in 1985 under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman.

Jarl Charpentier (1884–1935) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University and the University of Bonn under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and Hermann Jacobi, serving as Assistant Professor (1908), Deputy Professor (1925), and Professor (1927) at Uppsala.
Jaroslav Průšek (1906–1980) was a sinologist who studied at Charles University's Faculty of Arts (~1924–1928).

Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied at the University of Sydney (BA Honours, 2005) and the University of Oxford (DPhil, 2013) under Alexis Sanderson and Peter Oldmeadow. He held posts at Oxford (attested 2011) and SOAS (attested 2020).

Jason M. Wirth is a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki (attested 2017–2019) and became a professor of philosophy at Seattle University around 2005.
Jason Matthew McCombs works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a BS from the University of Michigan and a PhD from UCLA (2014) under Gregory Schopen, later serving as a lecturer at UCLA.

Jason Neelis works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He earned degrees from UT Austin and the University of Washington (PhD, 2001) under Richard G. Salomon, later serving as Associate Professor and Chair at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2013–2021).

Jason Protass specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick (attested 2015–2016) and held posts at Ryukoku University and Academia Sinica.

Jay Jasanoff is a linguist and Indologist who earned his bachelor's degree at Harvard (~1959–1963). He held faculty posts at UC Berkeley, Harvard (1970–1978; 1998–), and Cornell University as full professor in linguistics (~1978–1998).
